```bash
const TRAFFIC_LAYER_PREFIXES = ['Traffic - ', 'TrafficIncidents - '];

/**
 * Id of the layer the route polyline should be inserted before: the first
 * traffic overlay layer or the first text label, whichever comes first in
 * the style, so incidents/flow and labels all draw above the route.
 */
export function routeAnchorLayerId(layers: LayerSpecification[]): string | undefined {
  return layers.find(
    (l) => isLabelLayer(l) || TRAFFIC_LAYER_PREFIXES.some((p) => l.id.startsWith(p))
  )?.id;
}""","""/** Layer-id prefixes of the Orbis traffic overlays (flow and incidents). */
const TRAFFIC_LAYER_PREFIXES = ['Traffic - ', 'TrafficIncidents - '];

/**
 * In every Orbis basemap (with or without traffic) this layer sits right
 * after the road lines and immediately before the traffic overlays.
 */
const ROUTE_ANCHOR_LAYER_ID = 'Borders - Country';

/**
 * Id of the layer the route polyline should be inserted before, so that
 * traffic incidents/flow, borders and labels all draw above the route.
 *
 * The anchor must be the SAME id whether or not traffic overlays are on:
 * react-map-gl applies a changed `beforeId` (moveLayer) before the map has
 * switched styles, which fails against a not-yet-existing layer and leaves
 * the route layers dropped by the style diff. "Borders - Country" is
 * constant across variants; the fallbacks cover unknown styles.
 */
export function routeAnchorLayerId(layers: LayerSpecification[]): string | undefined {
  if (layers.some((l) => l.id === ROUTE_ANCHOR_LAYER_ID)) return ROUTE_ANCHOR_LAYER_ID;
  return layers.find(
    (l) => isLabelLayer(l) || TRAFFIC_LAYER_PREFIXES.some((p) => l.id.startsWith(p))
  )?.id;
}"""),
])
```

```bash
cat > src/utils/maneuverGlyph.ts <<'EOF'
/**
 * Compact glyph for a maneuver, keyed on NB's maneuver_type + modifier.
 * Shared by the directions list and the active-maneuver map marker.
 */
export interface ManeuverGlyph {
  glyph: string;
  /** CSS rotation in degrees (for gentle "keep left/right" offsets). */
  rotate?: number;
}

export function maneuverGlyph(type: string, modifier?: string): ManeuverGlyph {
  const t = type.toLowerCase();
  const mod = (modifier ?? '').toLowerCase();
  if (t === 'depart') return { glyph: '●' };
  if (t === 'arrive') return { glyph: '⚑' };
  if (t.includes('roundabout') || t.includes('rotary')) return { glyph: '↻' };
  if (t === 'merge') return { glyph: '⤵' };
  // "Keep left/right" (a fork with a slight modifier): a mildly offset
  // arrow — gentler than the 45° slight-turn arrows
  if (t === 'fork' && mod.includes('left')) return { glyph: '↑', rotate: -20 };
  if (t === 'fork' && mod.includes('right')) return { glyph: '↑', rotate: 20 };
  if (t === 'fork' || t.includes('ramp') || t === 'on ramp' || t === 'off ramp')
    return { glyph: '⑂' };
  if (t === 'uturn' || mod.includes('uturn')) return { glyph: '⤶' };
  if (mod.includes('sharp left')) return { glyph: '↰' };
  if (mod.includes('sharp right')) return { glyph: '↱' };
  if (mod.includes('slight left')) return { glyph: '↖' };
  if (mod.includes('slight right')) return { glyph: '↗' };
  if (mod.includes('left')) return { glyph: '←' };
  if (mod.includes('right')) return { glyph: '→' };
  if (t === 'continue' || t === 'new name' || mod.includes('straight'))
    return { glyph: '↑' };
  return { glyph: '•' };
}
EOF
cat > src/components/map/ActiveManeuverMarker.tsx <<'EOF'
/**
 * Marker at the maneuver selected in the directions list, showing the
 * same icon as the list entry.
 */
'use client';

import React from 'react';
import { Marker } from 'react-map-gl';
import { Box } from '@mui/material';
import { useAppSelector } from '@/store/hooks';
import { maneuverGlyph } from '@/utils/maneuverGlyph';

export const ActiveManeuverMarker: React.FC = () => {
  const navigation = useAppSelector((state) => state.route.navigation);
  const activeStep = useAppSelector((state) => state.route.activeStep);

  const step =
    activeStep !== null ? navigation?.steps.find((s) => s.index === activeStep) : undefined;
  if (!step || !Number.isFinite(step.location[0]) || !Number.isFinite(step.location[1])) {
    return null;
  }
  const glyph = maneuverGlyph(step.maneuverType, step.modifier);

  return (
    <Marker
      longitude={step.location[0]}
      latitude={step.location[1]}
      anchor="center"
      style={{ zIndex: 4, pointerEvents: 'none' }}
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-25T15:37:28.749Z)

Both items are done and committed; working tree clean, test tab closed.

**Route under traffic overlays — fixed properly (`7ad3c3e`)**
- My first anchor choice (the first traffic layer) hid the route entirely in the sequence you hit: with a route already on the map, toggling traffic changed the route's `beforeId`, and react-map-gl applies that change (`moveLayer`) *before* the map has switched styles — against a layer that doesn't exist yet. maplibre fires an error, the style diff then drops the route layers, and they're never re-added. The console showed exactly that: "Cannot move layer route-main before non-existing layer TrafficIncidents - No delay outline".
- The route is now anchored before **`Borders - Country`**, which I verified exists in all five basemaps with and without traffic, always right above the road lines and immediately below the traffic overlays. Because the id never changes between variants, there's no move race. Verified route-first → incidents on (route stays, red segments paint over it at Palisade) and incidents off again (route stays).

**Maneuver marker (`5e24921`)**
- Clicking a step in the Directions list still zooms to it and now shows a red circular marker at that maneuver with the same icon as the list entry (shared `maneuverGlyph` helper; active step kept in the route store and cleared with the navigation result).
- **Oriented to the route**: each step now carries the API's `bearing_before`/`bearing_after`; the icon is rotated by the approach heading, so e.g. a left-turn arrow ends up pointing the way the route actually leaves the turn (verified at Kennedy Boulevard: arrow points north-east along the exit road). Departures show a straight arrow along the initial heading; arrivals aren't rotated. The rotation is map-aligned, so it also follows the compass if the map is rotated.

`main` is three commits ahead of `origin/main` (route ordering fix ×2, maneuver marker) — not pushed or deployed until you ask.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-25T15:46:47.189Z)

Done — committed as `dfa907f`, working tree clean, test tab closed.

**Pause-to-preview while dragging a vertex** (`src/components/map/RouteVertices.tsx`)
- While you hold a route vertex, every pointer move restarts a 300 ms timer. If you pause that long, the dragged point is **inserted as a stop right then** (at the correct position in the stop sequence) and the existing debounced route calculation fires — so the re-routed polyline appears while you're still holding the handle.
- Further movement after that pause **moves the same stop** (no duplicates); another pause re-routes again. Releasing commits the final position. If you never pause, behaviour is exactly as before: the stop is inserted on release.
- Once the stop exists, the grey ghost marker gives way to the real numbered stop marker under your cursor. The `addWaypoint` reducer now accepts an optional `id` so the drag can track the stop it created.

**Verification caveat**: I could only exercise this by code path, not visually. In my automation tab Chrome had `requestAnimationFrame` suspended again, so the vertex layer's hover visibility never painted and the synthetic drag couldn't find a handle to grab; the insert/move logic it uses is the same one verified earlier for the plain drag. It's worth a quick manual try on your side: grab a vertex, hold still for a moment, and the route should redraw before you let go.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-25T15:54:40.935Z)

Done — committed as `03df89d`, working tree clean, test tab closed.

**Directions now follow the route**
- Once you've fetched directions, the route store marks them as "following" (`directionsFollowRoute`). Any change that produces a new route — routing options, added/removed/dragged waypoints, vertex drags, mode, avoid/exclude, departure time — makes `DirectionsPanel` re-fetch turn-by-turn for the new route automatically and re-render the panel. No more clicking Get Directions.
- Closing the Directions panel (its × button) stops the following; Reset/Clear route also clear it. Language changes already re-fetched and still do.
- Verified in a fresh tab: with directions open at "22 mi · 53 min · 23 steps", switching Route Type refreshed the panel to "18 mi · 1h 12min · 24 steps", and clicking the map to add a stop refreshed it again to "20 mi · 1h 34min · 34 steps" with the stop in the list — both without pressing the button.

One behaviour to be aware of: during a recalculation the old panel disappears briefly (stale steps are cleared with the old route) and returns as soon as the new directions arrive.

# Weather API

Source: https://docs.nextbillion.ai/map-data/weather-api

# Weather API

## Introduction

The NextBillion.ai Weather API delivers real-time as well as predicted weather information for a specified region. API response provides radar-based current and forecasted precipitation details, using GeoJSON polygons. These polygons delineate the areas affected by particular weather conditions across various time intervals.

GET

https://api.nextbillion.io/map/weather?key={your_api_key}&region={region}



### Request Parameters

| Name | Required | Format and Usage | Description |
|------|----------|------------------|-------------|
| `key` | Yes | Type: `string`<br>Format: 32 character alphanumeric string | A key is a unique identifier that is required to authenticate a request to the API. |
| `region` | Yes | Type: `string`<br>Allowed values: `europe`, `nam`, `usa`, `australia`, `latam` | Specifies the region for which the weather polygons are to be fetched. Allowed value details: `europe`: Europe; `nam`: North America; `usa`: United States of America; `australia`: Australia; `latam`: Latin Americas. |

### Response Schema

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `features` | array of object | A collection of [geoJSON features](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7946#section-3.3) containing weather condition details for the requested region. |
| `features[].bbox` | string | Specifies the bounding box, in format of min\_long, min\_lat, max\_long, max\_lat, containing the weather polygon. |
| `features[].geometry` | object | An object with geoJSON details of the weather polygon. The contents of this object follow the [geoJSON standard](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7946#section-3.2). |
| `features[].geometry.type` | string | Type of the geoJSON geometry. Will always be `Polygon`. |
| `features[].geometry.coordinates` | array of array of number | An array of coordinates in the \[longitude, latitude\] format, representing the polygon boundary. |
| `features[].id` | string | Specifies the geoJSON feature ID. |
| `features[].properties` | object | An object containing useful details about the weather pattern type, intensity and its impacted area. |
| `features[].properties.area` | number | Returns the area of the weather polygon in square kilometers (km²). |
| `features[].properties.category` | string | Returns the category of the weather polygon, e.g., "precip". The precipitation type is indicated in `type`. |
| `features[].properties.type` | string | Returns the type of the weather polygon. Supported values: `rain`, `snow`, `mixed` and `hail` |
| `features[].properties.children` | array of string | Returns a list of Feature-Ids that represent polygons of the same `category` and `type` with the next higher `level` which lie inside the given polygon. An empty array means no children. |
| `features[].properties.countries` | array of string | The list of countries, represented as [ISO 3166-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1) alpha-3 country codes, that intersect with the weather polygon. |
| `features[].properties.level` | number | Returns the level of the weather atom, i.e., a numeric value describing its magnitude. e.g. for the "precip” category, a level of “2.0” indicates the precipitation levels. |
| `features[].properties.parent` | string | A single Feature-Id that represents the polygon of the next lower `level` containing this weather polygon. An empty string means no parent. |
| `features[].properties.uniqueId` | string | A unique and stable ID of the current weather polygon. |
| `features[].type` | string | Indicates the type of [geoJSON structure](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7946#section-3.2). Will always be `Feature` . |
| `properties` | object | Contains time related details for the `FeatureCollection` returned. |
| `properties.creationTime` | string | Returns the time of the request in UTC as an ISO-8601-compliant date-time string of the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssTZD |
| `properties.forecastOffset` | string | Returns the forecast horizon of the weather polygon, in minutes. Zero represents present time. |
| `properties.rootTimeStamp` | string | Returns the time at which the weather polygons were measured/predicted in UTC as an ISO-8601-compliant date-time string of the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssTZD |
| `properties.timeStamp` | string | Returns the time of which the weather polygons refer to (may be in the future) in UTC as an ISO-8601-compliant date-time string of the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssTZD |
| `type` | string | Indicates the type of [geoJSON structure](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7946#section-3.3). Will always be `FeatureCollection` . |

### Sample Request

```bash
curl --location 'https://api.nextbillion.io/map/weather?key=<your_api_key>&region=europe'
```

### Sample Response

```json
{
    "features": [
        {
            "features": [
                {
                    "bbox": [
                        -1.61,
                        47.778,
                        0.009,
                        48.608
                    ],
                    "geometry": {
                        "coordinates": [
                            [
                                [
                                    -1.216,
                                    47.778
                                ],
                                [
                                    -1.116,
                                    47.778
                                ],
                                [
```

## API Query Limits

NextBillion.ai allows a maximum rate limit of 6000 queries per minute or 100 queries/second for continuous requests.
*Note*: We can increase the quota if needed on request. Contact [[EMAIL]](mailto:[EMAIL]) for more details.

## API Error Codes

| Response code | Description | Additional notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Normal success case. | Normal success case. |
| 400 | Input validation failed. | There is a missing or an invalid parameter or a parameter with an invalid value type is added to the request. |
| 401 | APIKEY not supplied or invalid | This error occurs when the wrong API key is passed in the request or the key is missing altogether. |
| 403 | APIKEY is valid but does not have access to requested resources | You might be querying for a geographical region which is not valid for your account or requesting a service which is not enabled for you. |
| 404 | Requested host/path not found | This error occurs when a malformed hostname is used. |
| 422 | Could not process the request | A feasible solution could not be generated for the given set of locations or parameter configuration. |
| 429 | Too many requests | QPM reached or API request count quota reached. |
| 500 | Internal Service error. | There was an internal issue with NextBillion.ai services. You can reach out to [[EMAIL]](mailto:[EMAIL]) for an explanation. |

```bash
/**
 * API Route: Proxy to the NextBillion.ai Weather API (radar precipitation
 * polygons for a region). Keeps the key server-side.
 */
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';

const NB_API_KEY = process.env.NEXTBILLION_API_KEY || '';
const NB_WEATHER_URL = 'https://api.nextbillion.io/map/weather';
const REGIONS = new Set(['europe', 'nam', 'usa', 'australia', 'latam']);

export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  if (!NB_API_KEY) {
    return NextResponse.json({ status: 'Error', msg: 'API key not configured' }, { status: 500 });
  }
  const region = request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('region') ?? '';
  if (!REGIONS.has(region)) {
    return NextResponse.json({ status: 'Error', msg: 'Invalid "region" parameter' }, { status: 400 });
  }
  try {
    const params = new URLSearchParams({ region, key: NB_API_KEY });
    const response = await fetch(`${NB_WEATHER_URL}?${params}`, {
      headers: { Accept: 'application/json' },
    });
    const data = await response.json();
    return NextResponse.json(data, {
      status: response.status,
      headers: { 'Cache-Control': 'no-store, max-age=0' },
    });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Weather API error:', error);
    return NextResponse.json({ status: 'Error', msg: 'Failed to fetch weather' }, { status: 500 });
  }
}
EOF

/**
 * NextBillion.ai Weather API client: radar-based precipitation polygons
 * for a region, prepared as a content layer (colour by precipitation type,
 * opacity by intensity level).
 */

export type WeatherRegion = 'europe' | 'nam' | 'usa' | 'australia' | 'latam';
export const WEATHER_REGIONS: WeatherRegion[] = ['usa', 'nam', 'latam', 'europe', 'australia'];

/** Fill colour per precipitation type. */
export const WEATHER_TYPE_COLORS: Record<string, string> = {
  rain: '#1e88e5',
  snow: '#7e57c2',
  mixed: '#8e24aa',
  hail: '#fb8c00',
};
const DEFAULT_COLOR = '#1e88e5';

/** Fill opacity for an intensity level (levels are nested, so they stack). */
function levelOpacity(level: number): number {
  if (level >= 25) return 0.55;
  if (level >= 7) return 0.42;
  if (level >= 2) return 0.3;
  if (level >= 0.5) return 0.2;
  return 0.12;
}

/** Suggests the region containing a [lng, lat] (defaults to USA). */
export function suggestWeatherRegion([lng, lat]: [number, number]): WeatherRegion {
  if (lat < -8 && lng > 100) return 'australia';
  if (lng > -32 && lng < 45 && lat > 34) return 'europe';
  if (lat < 15 && lng < -30) return 'latam';
  if (lat >= 24 && lat <= 50 && lng >= -125 && lng <= -66) return 'usa';
  return 'nam';
}

export interface WeatherLayerData {
  data: GeoJSON.FeatureCollection;
  /** Time the polygons refer to (ISO-8601, UTC). */
  timeStamp?: string;
  forecastOffsetMin?: number;
}

interface WeatherResponse {
  type?: string;
  features?: unknown[];
  properties?: { timeStamp?: string; forecastOffset?: number | string };
  status?: string;
  msg?: string;
}

const isFeatureCollection = (v: unknown): v is GeoJSON.FeatureCollection =>
  !!v && typeof v === 'object' && (v as { type?: string }).type === 'FeatureCollection';

/**
 * Fetches the current radar polygons for `region`. The API may return a
 * FeatureCollection directly or a list of FeatureCollections (one per
 * forecast offset); the present-time collection is used.
 */
export async function fetchWeatherLayer(region: WeatherRegion): Promise<WeatherLayerData> {
  const res = await fetch(`/api/weather?region=${encodeURIComponent(region)}`);
  const body: WeatherResponse = await res.json();
  if (!res.ok || (body.status && body.status !== 'Ok' && !body.features)) {
    throw new Error(body.msg ?? `Weather request failed (${res.status})`);
  }

  let collection: GeoJSON.FeatureCollection | null = null;
  let props = body.properties;
  const list = body.features ?? [];
  if (list.length && isFeatureCollection(list[0])) {
    const collections = list.filter(isFeatureCollection) as (GeoJSON.FeatureCollection & {
      properties?: WeatherResponse['properties'];
    })[];
    collection =
      collections.find((c) => Number(c.properties?.forecastOffset ?? 0) === 0) ?? collections[0];
    props = collection.properties;
  } else if (isFeatureCollection(body)) {
    collection = body;
  }
  if (!collection) throw new Error('Unexpected weather response');

  const features: GeoJSON.Feature[] = collection.features.map((f) => {
    const p = (f.properties ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
    const type = String(p.type ?? 'rain');
    const level = typeof p.level === 'number' ? p.level : 0;
    const { children: _children, parent: _parent, ...rest } = p; // eslint-disable-line @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars
    return {
      ...f,
      properties: {
        ...rest,
        __color: WEATHER_TYPE_COLORS[type] ?? DEFAULT_COLOR,
        __opacity: levelOpacity(level),
      },
    };
  });

  return {
    data: { type: 'FeatureCollection', features },
    timeStamp: props?.timeStamp,
    forecastOffsetMin: props?.forecastOffset !== undefined ? Number(props.forecastOffset) : undefined,
  };
}
```

```bash
sub('src/services/routing/geofenceApi.ts', [
("""interface CreateResponse {""","""/**
 * Shapes a polygon the way the Geofence API accepts it: a single closed
 * ring. Holes are dropped (the API rejects multi-ring polygons with
 * "geojson is not single polygon"), which only makes the avoid area
 * slightly larger.
 */
export function toGeofencePolygon(polygon: GeoJSON.Polygon): GeoJSON.Polygon {
  const ring = [...(polygon.coordinates[0] ?? [])];
  const first = ring[0];
  const last = ring[ring.length - 1];
  if (first && last && (first[0] !== last[0] || first[1] !== last[1])) ring.push(first);
  return { type: 'Polygon', coordinates: [ring] };
}

interface CreateResponse {"""),

/** Property carrying a feature's index (see buildContentLayer). */
export const FEATURE_INDEX_PROP = '__idx';

 * Builds a content layer, stamping every feature with its index so a map
 * hit can be traced back to the original (untiled, unsimplified) geometry.
 */
export function buildContentLayer(input: {
  name: string;
  data: GeoJSON.FeatureCollection;
  color: string;
  visible?: boolean;
  /** Omit to auto-detect from the data; null for "layer name". */
  titleField?: string | null;

      ...f,
      properties: { ...(f.properties ?? {}), [FEATURE_INDEX_PROP]: i },
    })),
  };
  const fields = collectFields(data);
  return {
    id: generateId(),
    name: input.name,
    color: input.color,
    visible: input.visible ?? true,
    featureCount: data.features.length,
    data,
    bounds: featureCollectionBounds(data),
    fields,
    popupEnabled: true,
    titleField:
      input.titleField !== undefined ? input.titleField : defaultTitleField(data, fields),
```

```bash
import { Close as CloseIcon, Fence as GeofenceIcon } from '@mui/icons-material';
import { useAppDispatch, useAppSelector } from '@/store/hooks';
import { useT } from '@/hooks/useT';
import {
  FEATURE_INDEX_PROP,
  type ContentLayer,
  type FeatureGeofence,
} from '@/utils/contentLayers';
import {
  MAX_GEOFENCES_PER_LAYER,
  createPolygonGeofence,
  deleteGeofence,
  extractPolygons,
  geofenceAvoidValue,
} from '@/services/routing/geofenceApi';"""),
("""  const { current: mapRef } = useMap();
  const layers = useAppSelector((state) => state.ui.contentLayers);

"""  const { current: mapRef } = useMap();
  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();
  const layers = useAppSelector((state) => state.ui.contentLayers);
  const featureGeofences = useAppSelector((state) => state.ui.featureGeofences);
  const { t, locale } = useT();
  const [geofenceBusy, setGeofenceBusy] = useState(false);
  const [geofenceError, setGeofenceError] = useState<string | null>(null);"""),
("""  const fields = (layer.popupFields ?? layer.fields).filter((f) => f !== layer.titleField);
  const close = () => {
    setPinned(false);
    setHovered(null);
  };""",
"""  const fields = (layer.popupFields ?? layer.fields).filter((f) => f !== layer.titleField);
  const close = () => {
    setPinned(false);
    setHovered(null);
  };

  // Geofence from this feature alone: only for areas we can trace back to
  // the layer's original geometry (map hits are tiled and simplified)
  const rawIdx = hovered.properties[FEATURE_INDEX_PROP];
  const featureIdx = typeof rawIdx === 'number' ? rawIdx : null;
  const sourceFeature = featureIdx !== null ? layer.data.features[featureIdx] : undefined;
  const polygons = sourceFeature
    ? extractPolygons({ type: 'FeatureCollection', features: [sourceFeature] }).slice(
        0,
        MAX_GEOFENCES_PER_LAYER
      )
    : [];
  const featureFences = featureGeofences.filter(
    (g) => g.layerId === layer.id && g.featureIdx === featureIdx
  );

  const createFeatureGeofence = async () => {
    if (featureIdx === null) return;
    setGeofenceBusy(true);
    setGeofenceError(null);
    const created: FeatureGeofence[] = [];
    try {
      for (const [i, polygon] of polygons.entries()) {
        const name = `${layer.name} · ${title}${polygons.length > 1 ? ` ${i + 1}` : ''}`.slice(
          0,
          120
        );
        created.push({
          id: await createPolygonGeofence(name, polygon),
          layerId: layer.id,
          featureIdx,
          name,
        });
      }
      dispatch.ui.addFeatureGeofences(created);
      for (const g of created) dispatch.routingOptions.addAvoid(geofenceAvoidValue(g.id));
    } catch (err) {
      // Don't leave half-created fences behind
      await Promise.all(created.map((g) => deleteGeofence(g.id)));
      setGeofenceError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));
    } finally {
      setGeofenceBusy(false);
    }
  };

  const removeFeatureGeofence = async () => {
    const ids = featureFences.map((g) => g.id);
    dispatch.routingOptions.removeAvoid(ids.map(geofenceAvoidValue));
    dispatch.ui.removeFeatureGeofences(ids);
    await Promise.all(ids.map(deleteGeofence));
  };"""),

          </Box>

          {/* Turn this feature into a routing avoid area */}
          {polygons.length > 0 && (

              {featureFences.length > 0 ? (
                <Box sx={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 1 }}>
                  <GeofenceIcon fontSize="small" color="success" />
                  <Typography variant="caption" sx={{ flex: 1 }}>
                    {t('layer.geofenceActive', { n: featureFences.length })}
                  </Typography>
                  <Button
                    size="small"
                    color="inherit"
                    onClick={() => void removeFeatureGeofence()}
                    sx={{ textTransform: 'none' }}
                  >
                    {t('layer.removeGeofence')}
                  </Button>
                </Box>
              ) : (
                <Button
                  size="small"
                  variant="outlined"
                  fullWidth
                  disabled={geofenceBusy}
                  startIcon={
                    geofenceBusy ? <CircularProgress size={14} /> : <GeofenceIcon />
                  }
                  onClick={() => void createFeatureGeofence()}
                  sx={{ textTransform: 'none' }}
                >
                  {t('layer.createFeatureGeofence')}
                </Button>
              )}
              {geofenceError && (
                <Typography variant="caption" color="error" display="block" sx={{ mt: 0.5 }}>
                  {t('layer.geofenceFailed', { error: geofenceError })}
                </Typography>
              )}
            </Box>
          )}
        </Box>
      </Popup>"""),
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-25T16:44:51.241Z)

Done — the weather overlay (`38e040f`) and the geofence action (`6269ed0`, plus the array-formatting fix `896fc11`) are committed; working tree clean, test tab closed, and the geofence I created while testing was removed through the UI (so nothing lingers in your NB account).

**Weather overlay** (Settings → Weather)
- Pick a region — pre-selected from the map centre — and **Add weather layer**: the radar precipitation polygons arrive as a normal content layer (toggle, info window, remove), coloured by precipitation type (rain/snow/mixed/hail) with fill opacity scaled by intensity level, so nested heavier cells read darker. The button becomes **Refresh weather** for a region already loaded, replacing the old layer. Key stays server-side via `/api/weather`.
- Note on the API: the live response is a flat `FeatureCollection` (the docs show a nested one), so the client accepts both shapes and picks the present-time collection when several forecast offsets come back.

**"Create geofence and avoid" in the feature popup**
- Hovering (or clicking) a weather polygon — or any polygon feature of any content layer — shows the info card with a **Create geofence and avoid** button. It creates a NextBillion geofence from *that one feature's* polygon and adds it to the routing **Avoid** list, where it appears as a chip ("Geofence: Weather · USA 12:30 PM"). The card then shows "Avoided in routing (1 geofence)" with **Remove geofence**, which drops the avoid and deletes the fence. Removing the layer (or refreshing weather) cleans up its feature geofences too, and a half-failed creation rolls back.
- Two API constraints I found and handled: rings must be closed (weather polygons arrive open), and polygons with holes are rejected ("geojson is not single polygon") — so the outer ring is sent, closed. Dropping holes only makes the avoided area slightly larger.
- To make the geofence use the true geometry rather than the tiled/simplified one under the cursor, content layers now stamp each feature with its index and the card looks the original up; layer construction is shared by imports, bundled layers and weather.
- Verified live at Saguenay: card → create → chip in Avoid → remove → back to normal, with `countries` now rendering as "CAN" rather than `["CAN"]`.

`main` is three commits ahead of `origin/main` — not pushed or deployed until you ask.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-25T16:58:38.278Z)

[tool: Bash — Add share URL codec, restore hook, store reducers]
```bash
cat > src/utils/shareUrl.ts <<'EOF'
/**
 * Shareable session links: the waypoints, routing options and map view are
 * encoded as readable query parameters so a link reproduces the session
 * (and can be hand-edited).
 *
 * Not included: uploaded content layers (file data) and geofence avoids,
 * which are server-side objects tied to the session that created them.
 */
import {
  AVOID_VALUES,
  DEFAULT_ROUTING_OPTIONS,
  EXCLUDE_VALUES,
  HAZMAT_TYPES,
  ROUTE_TYPES,
  TRAVEL_MODES,
  type AvoidOption,
  type ExcludeOption,
  type GeofenceAvoid,
  type HazmatType,
  type MapViewport,
  type RouteType,
  type RoutingOptions,
  type TravelMode,
  type Waypoint,
} from '@/types/routing';
import { DEFAULT_MAP_STYLE, MAP_STYLE_OPTIONS, type MapStyleId, type TrafficOverlays } from '@/utils/mapStyles';
import { DEFAULT_LOCALE, LOCALES, type Locale } from '@/i18n/locales';
import { isGeofenceAvoid } from '@/services/routing/geofenceApi';
import type { DistanceUnits } from '@/utils/formatting';
import { generateId } from '@/utils/formatting';

export interface ShareableSession {
  origin: Waypoint | null;
  destination: Waypoint | null;
  intermediates: Waypoint[];
  options: RoutingOptions;
  viewport: MapViewport;
  mapStyle: MapStyleId;
  traffic: TrafficOverlays;
  units: DistanceUnits;
  language: Locale;
}

const COORD_DECIMALS = 6;
const round = (n: number) => Number(n.toFixed(COORD_DECIMALS));
const isSet = (wp: Waypoint | null): wp is Waypoint =>
  !!wp && (wp.coordinates[0] !== 0 || wp.coordinates[1] !== 0);

/** "lat,lng[,name]" — the name may itself contain commas. */
function encodeWaypoint(wp: Waypoint): string {
  const [lng, lat] = wp.coordinates;
  const base = `${round(lat)},${round(lng)}`;
  return wp.name ? `${base},${wp.name}` : base;
}

function decodeWaypoint(raw: string, type: Waypoint['type']): Waypoint | null {
  const parts = raw.split(',');
  const lat = Number(parts[0]);
  const lng = Number(parts[1]);
  if (!Number.isFinite(lat) || !Number.isFinite(lng)) return null;
  const name = parts.slice(2).join(',').trim();
  return {
    id: generateId(),
    type,
    coordinates: [lng, lat],
    ...(name ? { name } : {}),
  };
}

const keep = <T extends string>(values: string[], allowed: T[]): T[] =>
  values.filter((v): v is T => (allowed as string[]).includes(v));

const positive = (raw: string | null): number | undefined => {
  const n = Number(raw);
  return raw !== null && Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : undefined;
};

/** Encodes a session; defaults are omitted to keep links short. */
export function buildShareParams(s: ShareableSession): URLSearchParams {
  const p = new URLSearchParams();
  if (isSet(s.origin)) p.set('o', encodeWaypoint(s.origin));
  if (isSet(s.destination)) p.set('d', encodeWaypoint(s.destination));
  const stops = s.intermediates.filter(isSet);
  if (stops.length) p.set('w', stops.map(encodeWaypoint).join('|'));

  const o = s.options;
  if (o.mode !== DEFAULT_ROUTING_OPTIONS.mode) p.set('mode', o.mode);
  if (o.routeType !== DEFAULT_ROUTING_OPTIONS.routeType) p.set('rt', o.routeType);
  // Geofence avoids reference server-side objects of this session only
  const avoid = o.avoid.filter((a) => !isGeofenceAvoid(a));
  if (avoid.length) p.set('avoid', avoid.join('|'));
  if (o.exclude.length) p.set('exclude', o.exclude.join('|'));
  if (o.departureTime) p.set('dep', String(Math.floor(o.departureTime.getTime() / 1000)));
  if (o.hazmatTypes.length) p.set('hazmat', o.hazmatTypes.join('|'));
  if (o.optimizeStops) p.set('opt', '1');
  if (o.truckWeight) p.set('tw', String(o.truckWeight));
  if (o.truckHeight) p.set('th', String(o.truckHeight));
  if (o.truckWidth) p.set('twd', String(o.truckWidth));
  if (o.truckLength) p.set('tl', String(o.truckLength));

  p.set('c', `${round(s.viewport.center[1])},${round(s.viewport.center[0])}`);
  p.set('z', s.viewport.zoom.toFixed(2));
  if (s.mapStyle !== DEFAULT_MAP_STYLE) p.set('style', s.mapStyle);
  const overlays = [s.traffic.flow ? 'flow' : '', s.traffic.incidents ? 'incidents' : ''].filter(
    Boolean
  );
  if (overlays.length) p.set('traffic', overlays.join('|'));
  if (s.units !== 'metric') p.set('units', s.units);
  if (s.language !== DEFAULT_LOCALE) p.set('lang', s.language);
  return p;
}

export function buildShareUrl(s: ShareableSession, base: string): string {
  const params = buildShareParams(s);
  const url = new URL(base);
  url.search = params.toString();
  url.hash = '';
  return url.toString();
}

export interface ParsedSession {
  origin?: Waypoint;
  destination?: Waypoint;
  intermediates?: Waypoint[];
  options?: Partial<RoutingOptions>;
  viewport?: Partial<MapViewport>;
  mapStyle?: MapStyleId;
  traffic?: TrafficOverlays;
  units?: DistanceUnits;
  language?: Locale;
}

/** Reads a session from query parameters; unknown/invalid values are ignored. */
export function parseShareParams(p: URLSearchParams): ParsedSession {
  const out: ParsedSession = {};

  const origin = p.get('o') ? decodeWaypoint(p.get('o')!, 'origin') : null;
  if (origin) out.origin = origin;
  const destination = p.get('d') ? decodeWaypoint(p.get('d')!, 'destination') : null;
  if (destination) out.destination = destination;
  const stops = (p.get('w') ?? '')
    .split('|')
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map((raw) => decodeWaypoint(raw, 'waypoint'))
    .filter((wp): wp is Waypoint => !!wp);
  if (stops.length) out.intermediates = stops;

  const options: Partial<RoutingOptions> = {};
  const mode = p.get('mode');
  if (mode && (TRAVEL_MODES as string[]).includes(mode)) options.mode = mode as TravelMode;
  const rt = p.get('rt');
  if (rt && (ROUTE_TYPES as string[]).includes(rt)) options.routeType = rt as RouteType;
  if (p.has('avoid')) {
    options.avoid = keep<AvoidOption>(p.get('avoid')!.split('|'), AVOID_VALUES) as (
      | AvoidOption
      | GeofenceAvoid
    )[];
  }
  if (p.has('exclude')) {
    options.exclude = keep<ExcludeOption>(p.get('exclude')!.split('|'), EXCLUDE_VALUES);
  }
  if (p.has('hazmat')) {
    options.hazmatTypes = keep<HazmatType>(p.get('hazmat')!.split('|'), HAZMAT_TYPES);
  }
  const dep = Number(p.get('dep'));
  if (p.has('dep') && Number.isFinite(dep) && dep > 0) options.departureTime = new Date(dep * 1000);
  if (p.has('opt')) options.optimizeStops = p.get('opt') === '1';
  const truckWeight = positive(p.get('tw'));
  if (truckWeight) options.truckWeight = truckWeight;
  const truckHeight = positive(p.get('th'));
  if (truckHeight) options.truckHeight = truckHeight;
  const truckWidth = positive(p.get('twd'));
  if (truckWidth) options.truckWidth = truckWidth;
  const truckLength = positive(p.get('tl'));
  if (truckLength) options.truckLength = truckLength;
  if (Object.keys(options).length) out.options = options;

  const center = (p.get('c') ?? '').split(',');
  const lat = Number(center[0]);
  const lng = Number(center[1]);
  const zoom = Number(p.get('z'));
  const viewport: Partial<MapViewport> = {};
  if (Number.isFinite(lat) && Number.isFinite(lng) && center.length === 2) {
    viewport.center = [lng, lat];
  }
  if (p.has('z') && Number.isFinite(zoom)) viewport.zoom = zoom;
  if (Object.keys(viewport).length) out.viewport = viewport;

  const style = p.get('style');
  if (style && MAP_STYLE_OPTIONS.some((o) => o.id === style)) out.mapStyle = style as MapStyleId;
  if (p.has('traffic')) {
    const overlays = p.get('traffic')!.split('|');
    out.traffic = { flow: overlays.includes('flow'), incidents: overlays.includes('incidents') };
  }
  const units = p.get('units');
  if (units === 'metric' || units === 'imperial') out.units = units;
  const language = p.get('lang');
  if (language && LOCALES.some((l) => l.id === language)) out.language = language as Locale;

  return out;
}

/** True when the URL carries any session parameter. */
export function hasShareParams(p: URLSearchParams): boolean {
  for (const key of ['o', 'd', 'w', 'mode', 'rt', 'avoid', 'exclude', 'dep', 'hazmat', 'c', 'style']) {
    if (p.has(key)) return true;
  }
  return false;
}
EOF
cat > src/hooks/useShareableUrl.ts <<'EOF'
/**
 * Restores a session from the URL's query parameters on first load, so a
 * shared link reproduces the waypoints, routing options and map view.
 */
'use client';

import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { useAppDispatch } from '@/store/hooks';
import { hasShareParams, parseShareParams } from '@/utils/shareUrl';

// Guard against React's double-invoked effects in development
let restored = false;

export function useShareableUrl() {
  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();

  useEffect(() => {
    if (restored || typeof window === 'undefined') return;
    restored = true;

    const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    if (!hasShareParams(params)) return;
    const s = parseShareParams(params);

    // Display settings first, so the rest renders in the shared locale
    if (s.units) dispatch.ui.setUnits(s.units);
    if (s.language) dispatch.ui.setLanguage(s.language);
    if (s.mapStyle) dispatch.ui.setMapStyle(s.mapStyle);
    if (s.traffic) dispatch.ui.setTraffic(s.traffic);
    if (s.viewport) dispatch.ui.setMapViewport(s.viewport);

    if (s.options) dispatch.routingOptions.setOptions(s.options);
    if (s.origin || s.destination || s.intermediates) {
      dispatch.waypoints.setAll({
        origin: s.origin ?? null,
        destination: s.destination ?? null,
        intermediates: s.intermediates ?? [],
      });
    }
  }, [dispatch]);
}
```

```bash
/**
 * Polygon draw / edit toggle — a native maplibre control so it stacks with
 * the navigation and traffic controls.
 */
'use client';

import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { useControl } from 'react-map-gl';
import type { IControl } from 'maplibre-gl';

export type DrawMode = 'idle' | 'draw' | 'edit';

// Pentagon outline (draw) and Material "edit" pencil (reshape)
const DRAW_ICON_SVG = `
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round" style="display:block">
  <path d="M12 3 4 9.5 7 19h10l3-9.5z"/>
</svg>`;
const EDIT_ICON_SVG = `
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" style="display:block">
  <path d="M3 17.25V21h3.75L17.81 9.94l-3.75-3.75L3 17.25zM20.71 7.04c.39-.39.39-1.02 0-1.41l-2.34-2.34a.9959.9959 0 00-1.41 0l-1.83 1.83 3.75 3.75 1.83-1.83z"/>
</svg>`;

export interface DrawControlLabels {
  draw: string;
  stopDrawing: string;
  edit: string;
  stopEditing: string;
  noAreas: string;
}

class PolygonDrawControl implements IControl {
  private container: HTMLDivElement | null = null;
  private drawButton: HTMLButtonElement | null = null;
  private editButton: HTMLButtonElement | null = null;

  constructor(private onSelect: (mode: DrawMode) => void) {}

  onAdd(): HTMLElement {
    this.container = document.createElement('div');
    this.container.className = 'maplibregl-ctrl maplibregl-ctrl-group';

    const make = (icon: string, onClick: () => void) => {
      const button = document.createElement('button');
      button.type = 'button';
      button.style.display = 'flex';
      button.style.alignItems = 'center';
      button.style.justifyContent = 'center';
      button.innerHTML = icon;
      button.addEventListener('click', onClick);
      this.container!.appendChild(button);
      return button;
    };

    this.drawButton = make(DRAW_ICON_SVG, () => this.onSelect('draw'));
    this.editButton = make(EDIT_ICON_SVG, () => this.onSelect('edit'));
    return this.container;
  }

  onRemove(): void {
    this.container?.remove();
    this.container = null;
    this.drawButton = null;
    this.editButton = null;
  }

  setState(mode: DrawMode, canEdit: boolean, labels: DrawControlLabels): void {
    if (this.drawButton) {
      const active = mode === 'draw';
      this.drawButton.title = active ? labels.stopDrawing : labels.draw;
      this.drawButton.setAttribute('aria-label', labels.draw);
      this.drawButton.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(active));
      this.drawButton.style.color = active ? '#1976D2' : '#616161';
    }
    if (this.editButton) {
      const active = mode === 'edit';
      this.editButton.disabled = !canEdit;
      this.editButton.title = !canEdit
        ? labels.noAreas
        : active
          ? labels.stopEditing
          : labels.edit;
      this.editButton.setAttribute('aria-label', labels.edit);
      this.editButton.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(active));
      this.editButton.style.color = active ? '#1976D2' : '#616161';
      this.editButton.style.opacity = canEdit ? '1' : '0.4';
    }
  }
}

interface DrawControlProps {
  mode: DrawMode;
  canEdit: boolean;
  labels: DrawControlLabels;
  /** Called with the button's mode; selecting the active mode turns it off. */
  onSelect: (mode: DrawMode) => void;
}

export function DrawControl({ mode, canEdit, labels, onSelect }: DrawControlProps) {
  const onSelectRef = useRef(onSelect);
  onSelectRef.current = onSelect;

  const control = useControl<PolygonDrawControl>(
    () => new PolygonDrawControl((m) => onSelectRef.current(m)),
    { position: 'top-right' }
  );

  useEffect(() => {
    control.setState(mode, canEdit, labels);
  }, [control, mode, canEdit, labels]);

  return null;
}

export default DrawControl;

cat > src/components/map/PolygonDrawTool.tsx <<'EOF'
/**
 * Draws and edits polygons on the map. Finished areas are appended to a
 * "drawn" content layer, so they get the same rendering, info window
 * (including "Create geofence and avoid") and visibility toggle as
 * imported layers.
 *
 * Draw: click to add points, click the first point / double-click / Enter
 * to close, Esc to cancel. Edit: drag a point to reshape.
 */
'use client';

import React, { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { Layer, Marker, Source, useMap } from 'react-map-gl';
import type { CircleLayer, FillLayer, LineLayer } from 'react-map-gl';
import type { Map as MaplibreMap, MapMouseEvent } from 'maplibre-gl';
import { Box } from '@mui/material';
import { useAppDispatch, useAppSelector } from '@/store/hooks';
import { useT } from '@/hooks/useT';
import { buildContentLayer, type ContentLayer } from '@/utils/contentLayers';
import { deleteGeofence, geofenceAvoidValue } from '@/services/routing/geofenceApi';

/** Colour of the drawn-areas layer and the in-progress outline. */
export const DRAWN_LAYER_COLOR = '#d81b60';
const DRAFT_SOURCE_ID = 'polygon-draft';
/** Click within this many pixels of the first point to close the ring. */
const CLOSE_PX = 12;

type Position = [number, number];

const draftLine: LineLayer = {
  id: 'polygon-draft-line',
  type: 'line',
  source: DRAFT_SOURCE_ID,
  layout: { 'line-cap': 'round', 'line-join': 'round' },
  paint: { 'line-color': DRAWN_LAYER_COLOR, 'line-width': 2.5, 'line-dasharray': [2, 1.5] },
};
const draftFill: FillLayer = {
  id: 'polygon-draft-fill',
  type: 'fill',
  source: DRAFT_SOURCE_ID,
  filter: ['==', ['geometry-type'], 'Polygon'],
  paint: { 'fill-color': DRAWN_LAYER_COLOR, 'fill-opacity': 0.15 },
};
const draftPoints: CircleLayer = {
  id: 'polygon-draft-points',
  type: 'circle',
  source: DRAFT_SOURCE_ID,
  filter: ['==', ['geometry-type'], 'Point'],
  paint: {
    'circle-radius': 4,
    'circle-color': '#fff',
    'circle-stroke-color': DRAWN_LAYER_COLOR,
    'circle-stroke-width': 2,
  },
};

/** Ring (closed) from the points drawn so far. */
function closedRing(points: Position[]): Position[] {
  const ring = [...points];
  const first = ring[0];
  const last = ring[ring.length - 1];
  if (first && last && (first[0] !== last[0] || first[1] !== last[1])) ring.push(first);
  return ring;
}

interface PolygonDrawToolProps {
  /** Set when the tool consumes a click so no waypoint is added. */
  suppressClickRef: React.MutableRefObject<boolean>;
  /** Flags marker interactions so the map ignores the click that follows. */
  onMarkerInteraction: () => void;
}

export const PolygonDrawTool: React.FC<PolygonDrawToolProps> = ({
  suppressClickRef,
  onMarkerInteraction,
}) => {
  const { current: mapRef } = useMap();
  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();
  const { t } = useT();
  const mode = useAppSelector((state) => state.ui.drawMode);
  const layers = useAppSelector((state) => state.ui.contentLayers);
  const featureGeofences = useAppSelector((state) => state.ui.featureGeofences);
  const drawnLayer = layers.find((l) => l.drawn);

  const [points, setPoints] = useState<Position[]>([]);
  const [cursor, setCursor] = useState<Position | null>(null);

  // Latest values for the map handlers (registered once per mode)
  const latest = useRef({ points, drawnLayer, suppressClickRef, dispatch, t });
  latest.current = { points, drawnLayer, suppressClickRef, dispatch, t };

  /** Appends a finished polygon to the drawn layer (creating it if needed). */
  const commitPolygon = useCallback((ring: Position[]) => {
    const { drawnLayer: layer, dispatch: d, t: translate } = latest.current;
    const index = (layer?.data.features.length ?? 0) + 1;
    const feature: GeoJSON.Feature = {
      type: 'Feature',
      properties: { name: translate('draw.areaName', { n: index }), points: ring.length - 1 },
      geometry: { type: 'Polygon', coordinates: [ring] },
    };
    if (layer) {
      d.ui.setContentLayerFeatures({
        id: layer.id,
        features: [...layer.data.features, feature],
      });
    } else {
      d.ui.addContentLayers([
        buildContentLayer({
          name: translate('draw.layerName'),
          data: { type: 'FeatureCollection', features: [feature] },
          color: DRAWN_LAYER_COLOR,
          titleField: 'name',
          drawn: true,
        }),
      ]);
    }
  }, []);

  // Drawing interactions
  useEffect(() => {
    const map = mapRef?.getMap() as unknown as MaplibreMap | undefined;
    if (!map || mode !== 'draw') return;

    // A double-click finishes the ring rather than zooming
    map.doubleClickZoom.disable();

    const finish = () => {
      const ring = closedRing(latest.current.points);
      if (ring.length >= 4) commitPolygon(ring);
      setPoints([]);
      setCursor(null);
    };
    const cancel = () => {
      setPoints([]);
      setCursor(null);
    };

    const onMouseDown = () => {
      // Consumed before the map's own click handler adds a waypoint
      latest.current.suppressClickRef.current = true;
    };
    const onClick = (e: MapMouseEvent) => {
      const current = latest.current.points;
      const first = current[0];
      if (first && current.length >= 3) {
        const p = map.project(first);
        if (Math.hypot(p.x - e.point.x, p.y - e.point.y) <= CLOSE_PX) {
          finish();
          return;
        }
      }
      setPoints([...current, [e.lngLat.lng, e.lngLat.lat]]);
    };
    const onMouseMove = (e: MapMouseEvent) => setCursor([e.lngLat.lng, e.lngLat.lat]);
    const onDblClick = (e: MapMouseEvent) => {
      e.preventDefault();
      finish();
    };
    const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (e.key === 'Enter') finish();
      else if (e.key === 'Escape') cancel();
    };

    map.on('mousedown', onMouseDown);
    map.on('click', onClick);
    map.on('mousemove', onMouseMove);
    map.on('dblclick', onDblClick);
    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);
    return () => {
      map.off('mousedown', onMouseDown);
      map.off('click', onClick);
      map.off('mousemove', onMouseMove);
      map.off('dblclick', onDblClick);
      window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);
      map.doubleClickZoom.enable();
      setPoints([]);
      setCursor(null);
    };
  }, [mapRef, mode, commitPolygon]);

  /** Reshaping invalidates any geofence made from that area. */
  const dropGeofencesFor = useCallback(
    (layer: ContentLayer, featureIdx: number) => {
      const stale = featureGeofences.filter(
        (g) => g.layerId === layer.id && g.featureIdx === featureIdx
      );
      if (!stale.length) return;
      const ids = stale.map((g) => g.id);
      dispatch.routingOptions.removeAvoid(ids.map(geofenceAvoidValue));
      dispatch.ui.removeFeatureGeofences(ids);
      void Promise.all(ids.map(deleteGeofence));
    },
    [featureGeofences, dispatch]
  );

  const moveVertex = (
    layer: ContentLayer,
    featureIdx: number,
    vertexIdx: number,
    lngLat: Position
  ) => {
    const features = layer.data.features.map((f, i) => {
      if (i !== featureIdx || f.geometry.type !== 'Polygon') return f;
      const ring = [...f.geometry.coordinates[0]];
      ring[vertexIdx] = lngLat;
      // The closing point mirrors the first
      if (vertexIdx === 0) ring[ring.length - 1] = lngLat;
      return { ...f, geometry: { ...f.geometry, coordinates: [ring, ...f.geometry.coordinates.slice(1)] } };
    });
    dispatch.ui.setContentLayerFeatures({ id: layer.id, features });
    dropGeofencesFor(layer, featureIdx);
  };

  // In-progress ring: the closed polygon once it can be one, plus its points
  const draft: GeoJSON.FeatureCollection = {
    type: 'FeatureCollection',
    features: [],
  };
  if (mode === 'draw' && points.length) {
    const line = cursor ? [...points, cursor] : points;
    draft.features.push({
      type: 'Feature',
      properties: {},
      geometry: { type: 'LineString', coordinates: line },
    });
    if (points.length >= 3) {
      draft.features.push({
        type: 'Feature',
        properties: {},
        geometry: { type: 'Polygon', coordinates: [closedRing(line)] },
      });
    }
    for (const p of points) {
      draft.features.push({
        type: 'Feature',
        properties: {},
        geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: p },
      });
    }
  }

  return (
    <>
      {mode === 'draw' && (
        <Source id={DRAFT_SOURCE_ID} type="geojson" data={draft}>
          <Layer {...draftFill} />
          <Layer {...draftLine} />
          <Layer {...draftPoints} />
        </Source>
      )}

      {/* Editable vertices of the drawn areas */}
      {mode === 'edit' &&
        drawnLayer?.visible &&
        drawnLayer.data.features.flatMap((f, featureIdx) => {
          if (f.geometry.type !== 'Polygon') return [];
          const ring = f.geometry.coordinates[0] ?? [];
          // The closing point duplicates the first
          return ring.slice(0, -1).map((position, vertexIdx) => (
            <Marker
              key={`${featureIdx}-${vertexIdx}`}
              longitude={position[0]}
              latitude={position[1]}
              anchor="center"
              draggable
              onDragStart={onMarkerInteraction}
              onDrag={onMarkerInteraction}
              onDragEnd={(e) => {
                onMarkerInteraction();
                moveVertex(drawnLayer, featureIdx, vertexIdx, [e.lngLat.lng, e.lngLat.lat]);
              }}
              style={{ zIndex: 5 }}
            >
              <Box
                sx={{
                  width: 14,
                  height: 14,
                  borderRadius: '50%',
                  bgcolor: '#fff',
                  border: `3px solid ${DRAWN_LAYER_COLOR}`,
                  boxShadow: '0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)',
                  cursor: 'grab',
                  '&:active': { cursor: 'grabbing' },
                }}
              />
            </Marker>
          ));
        })}
    </>
  );
};

export default PolygonDrawTool;
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-25T17:16:13.416Z)

Done — built, deployed, committed and pushed.

**Polygon draw & edit tool (`91cc233`)**
- Two new buttons in the map control stack: **Draw polygon** (pentagon) and **Reshape areas** (pencil, enabled once an area exists).
- **Drawing**: click to drop points with a live dashed preview and a translucent fill once it can close; finish by clicking the first point, double-clicking, or pressing Enter; Esc cancels. The map hint switches to explain the mode, and clicks don't drop waypoints while drawing.
- **Editing**: drag any vertex to reshape; the hint reads "Drag a point to reshape an area".
- Finished areas land in a **"Drawn areas" content layer**, so they inherit everything that layer machinery already gives: rendering, visibility toggle in Settings, the feature info window, and **"Create geofence and avoid"** — plus a **Delete area** action of their own.
- Reshaping or deleting an area invalidates any geofence made from it: the fence is deleted server-side and dropped from Avoid (remaining feature geofences are re-indexed so they still point at the right shapes). POI/incident/layer cards and the route-vertex tool stand down while drawing or editing so they don't compete for clicks.
- Verified live in the browser: drew a 4-point area over NYC → Enter closed it → card showed "Drawn areas / Area 1, points 4" → "Create geofence and avoid" put "Geofence: Drawn areas · Area 1" in the Avoid list → dragging a vertex to Brooklyn reshaped it and cleared the stale geofence (Avoid back to None, fence deleted).

**Shipped**: `main` pushed to GitHub (`bfe7046..91cc233` — this also carried the shareable-links commit `b4c2915` from the previous turn); image `…:91cc233-draw` built, pushed and rolled out to Cloud Run (1 resource changed). Live at https://routing-playground-7j5cx7inrq-uc.a.run.app (HTTP 200).

One known limit worth mentioning: drawn areas live in the session only — they aren't persisted or encoded in share links (share links carry points and routing options, not layer geometry). Say the word if you'd like drawn areas persisted or shareable too.

```bash
cat > src/store/persistSession.ts <<'EOF'
/**
 * Persists the parts of a session that represent user work: areas drawn on
 * the map, imported GeoJSON/Shapefile layers, the geofences created from
 * them and the routing avoids that reference those geofences.
 *
 * Not persisted: weather layers (time-sensitive — refetch them) and the
 * bundled layers from /public (reloaded on startup; only their visibility
 * is remembered).
 */
import type { ContentLayer, FeatureGeofence } from '@/utils/contentLayers';
import { isGeofenceAvoid } from '@/services/routing/geofenceApi';

export const SESSION_STORAGE_KEY = 'nb-routing-playground.session';
/** Keep the stored blob well inside a typical 5 MB localStorage quota. */
const MAX_BYTES = 2_000_000;

export interface PersistedSession {
  layers: ContentLayer[];
  featureGeofences: FeatureGeofence[];
  /** Avoid entries of the form "geofence_id:<id>". */
  geofenceAvoids: string[];
  /** Visibility of the bundled layers, keyed by name. */
  bundledVisibility: Record<string, boolean>;
}

const EMPTY: PersistedSession = {
  layers: [],
  featureGeofences: [],
  geofenceAvoids: [],
  bundledVisibility: {},
};

function isLayer(v: unknown): v is ContentLayer {
  const l = v as ContentLayer | null;
  return (
    !!l &&
    typeof l === 'object' &&
    typeof l.id === 'string' &&
    typeof l.name === 'string' &&
    !!l.data &&
    l.data.type === 'FeatureCollection' &&
    Array.isArray(l.data.features)
  );
}

function isGeofence(v: unknown): v is FeatureGeofence {
  const g = v as FeatureGeofence | null;
  return (
    !!g &&
    typeof g === 'object' &&
    typeof g.id === 'string' &&
    typeof g.layerId === 'string' &&
    typeof g.featureIdx === 'number'
  );
}

/** Reads a saved session; anything malformed is dropped. */
export function loadSession(): PersistedSession {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return EMPTY;
  try {
    const raw = window.localStorage.getItem(SESSION_STORAGE_KEY);
    if (!raw) return EMPTY;
    const data = JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<PersistedSession>;
    const bundled = data.bundledVisibility;
    return {
      layers: Array.isArray(data.layers) ? data.layers.filter(isLayer) : [],
      featureGeofences: Array.isArray(data.featureGeofences)
        ? data.featureGeofences.filter(isGeofence)
        : [],
      geofenceAvoids: Array.isArray(data.geofenceAvoids)
        ? data.geofenceAvoids.filter((a): a is string => typeof a === 'string' && isGeofenceAvoid(a))
        : [],
      bundledVisibility:
        bundled && typeof bundled === 'object'
          ? Object.fromEntries(
              Object.entries(bundled).filter(([, v]) => typeof v === 'boolean')
            )
          : {},
    };
  } catch {
    return EMPTY;
  }
}

/**
 * Saves the session. Imported layers are dropped largest-first if the blob
 * would be too big; drawn areas are always kept (they only exist here).
 */
export function saveSession(
  layers: ContentLayer[],
  featureGeofences: FeatureGeofence[],
  avoid: string[]
): void {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return;

  const keep = layers.filter((l) => l.source === 'drawn' || l.source === 'imported');
  const bundledVisibility = Object.fromEntries(
    layers.filter((l) => l.source === 'bundled').map((l) => [l.name, l.visible])
  );
  const session: PersistedSession = {
    layers: keep,
    featureGeofences,
    geofenceAvoids: avoid.filter(isGeofenceAvoid),
    bundledVisibility,
  };

  let payload = JSON.stringify(session);
  if (payload.length > MAX_BYTES) {
    // Shed the biggest imported layers until it fits
    const sized = session.layers
      .map((l) => ({ l, size: JSON.stringify(l).length }))
      .sort((a, b) => b.size - a.size);
    const dropped: string[] = [];
    while (payload.length > MAX_BYTES && sized.length) {
      const biggest = sized.find((s) => s.l.source === 'imported');
      if (!biggest) break;
      sized.splice(sized.indexOf(biggest), 1);
      dropped.push(biggest.l.name);
      session.layers = session.layers.filter((l) => l.id !== biggest.l.id);
      payload = JSON.stringify(session);
    }
    if (dropped.length) {
      console.warn(`Content layers too large to remember: ${dropped.join(', ')}`);
    }
  }

  try {
    window.localStorage.setItem(SESSION_STORAGE_KEY, payload);
  } catch {
    // Quota exceeded or storage disabled: the session stays in memory
  }
}

cat > src/components/providers/SessionPersistence.tsx <<'EOF'
/**
 * Restores drawn areas, imported layers and their geofence avoids on load,
 * and saves them again whenever they change. Renders nothing.
 */
'use client';

import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { useAppDispatch, useAppSelector } from '@/store/hooks';
import { loadSession, saveSession } from '@/store/persistSession';
import { geofenceAvoidValue } from '@/services/routing/geofenceApi';
import type { GeofenceAvoid } from '@/types/routing';

/** Writes are debounced so dragging a vertex doesn't hammer localStorage. */
const SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS = 500;

export function SessionPersistence() {
  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();
  const contentLayers = useAppSelector((state) => state.ui.contentLayers);
  const featureGeofences = useAppSelector((state) => state.ui.featureGeofences);
  const avoid = useAppSelector((state) => state.routingOptions.avoid);
  const restored = useRef(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    const session = loadSession();
    if (session.layers.length) dispatch.ui.addContentLayers(session.layers);
    if (session.featureGeofences.length) {
      dispatch.ui.addFeatureGeofences(session.featureGeofences);
    }
    for (const value of session.geofenceAvoids) {
      // Stored as full "geofence_id:<id>" values
      dispatch.routingOptions.addAvoid(value as GeofenceAvoid);
    }
    // Layer-level geofences are restored with their layer
    for (const layer of session.layers) {
      for (const id of layer.geofenceIds ?? []) {
        dispatch.routingOptions.addAvoid(geofenceAvoidValue(id));
      }
    }
    restored.current = true;
  }, [dispatch]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!restored.current) return;
    const timer = setTimeout(
      () => saveSession(contentLayers, featureGeofences, avoid),
      SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS
    );
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  }, [contentLayers, featureGeofences, avoid]);

  return null;
}

export default SessionPersistence;
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-25T18:41:06.699Z)

Done — committed as `0017e01`, working tree clean, test tab closed and my test artifacts removed (drawn area deleted, its geofence deleted server-side).

**What now persists** (localStorage, key `nb-routing-playground.session`, alongside the existing settings key)
- **Drawn areas** — full geometry and their layer settings; they reappear on the map after a reload.
- **Imported layers** (GeoJSON / Shapefile uploads) — with a ~2 MB budget: if the blob would be too big, the largest *imported* layers are shed (with a console note); drawn areas are never shed, since they exist nowhere else.
- **Geofences and their avoids** — both per-feature geofences and layer-level ones, plus the matching `geofence_id:…` entries in the Avoid list, so routing still avoids them after a reload.
- **Bundled layer visibility** — the `/public` shapefiles reload from disk each time, so only their on/off state is remembered.
- **Not persisted**: weather layers (time-sensitive — refresh them), matching how the refresh button already works.

**Supporting changes**: layers now carry an explicit `source` (`imported` / `drawn` / `bundled` / `weather`) instead of the ad-hoc `drawn` flag; shared links no longer wipe geofence avoids when they apply their options; deleting the last drawn area removes the now-empty layer; and saves are debounced 500 ms so dragging a vertex doesn't hammer storage.

**Verified**: drew an area → created a geofence from it → reloaded → polygon back on the map, "Drawn areas · 1 features" in Settings, "Geofence: Drawn areas · Area 1" still in Avoid, no duplicates; then deleted the area and confirmed storage dropped to 388 bytes with no stray fences.

`main` is one commit ahead of `origin/main` — say the word and I'll push and deploy.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

### CLAUDE (2026-09-01T14:22:29.360Z)

Both done and committed.

**1. `road_info=traffic_light,stop_sign`** — every flexible request (Directions and Navigation share `buildParams`) now sends `road_info=toll_cost,traffic_light,stop_sign`. The API returns them on `routes[0].road_info` as `[{offset, latitude, longitude}]`; these are parsed into `RouteResult.trafficLights` / `.stopSigns` (`RoadPoint[]` with `offset` + `[lng,lat]`), and the counts show as a caption row in the Route Summary card (i18n'd across all 14 locales).

One thing worth knowing: the **default key (`45c1b3…`) is not provisioned for these** — it returns 200 with no `traffic_light`/`stop_sign` in `road_info`. The hazmat key (`[REDACTED_SECRET]…`) is, so the counts only render today when a hazmat route swaps keys server-side. Verified live: EWR-style LA route in truck+hazmat mode showed "Traffic lights: 14". Worth asking NB to enable it on the main key.

**2. Sidebar scroll** — the sidebar's scroll container is a flex column, so the panels were shrinking to fit rather than overflowing: measured in the browser, the API Response panel was crushed from 291px to 115px and `scrollHeight === clientHeight` (no scroll at all). Fixed with `'& > *': { flexShrink: 0 }` plus `minHeight: 0` on the container; it now scrolls to the full panel.

Not deployed — say the word and I'll run the build/deploy/push cycle.

```bash
"""    /**
     * Records the current waypoints so the next map edit can be undone.
     * Call this immediately before an edit made on the map (click to add a
     * stop, marker drag, or a route-vertex drag).
     */
    checkpoint(state) {
      const history = [...state.history, snapshot(state)];
      return {
        ...state,
        history: history.slice(-HISTORY_LIMIT),
      };
    },

    /** Restores the most recent checkpoint; a no-op with nothing to undo. */
    undo(state) {
      const previous = state.history[state.history.length - 1];
      if (!previous) return state;
      return {
        ...previous,
        history: state.history.slice(0, -1),
      };
    },

    clearAll(_state) {""",1)
```

```json
 "content": "/**\n * Undo button for map edits — a native maplibre control so it stacks with\n * the navigation, traffic and draw controls.\n */\n'use client';\n\nimport { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';\nimport { useControl } from 'react-map-gl';\nimport type { IControl } from 'maplibre-gl';\n\n// Material \"undo\" arrow\nconst UNDO_ICON_SVG = `\n<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"20\" height=\"20\" viewBox=\"0 0 24 24\" fill=\"currentColor\" style=\"display:block\">\n  <path d=\"M12.5 8c-2.65 0-5.05.99-6.9 2.6L2 7v9h9l-3.62-3.62c1.39-1.16 3.16-1.88 5.12-1.88 3.54 0 6.55 2.31 7.6 5.5l2.37-.78C21.08 11.03 17.15 8 12.5 8z\"/>\n</svg>`;\n\nexport interface UndoControlLabels {\n  undo: string;\n  nothingToUndo: string;\n}\n\nclass UndoMapControl implements IControl {\n  private container: HTMLDivElement | null = null;\n  private button: HTMLButtonElement | null = null;\n\n  constructor(private onUndo: () => void) {}\n\n  onAdd(): HTMLElement {\n    this.container = document.createElement('div');\n    this.container.className = 'maplibregl-ctrl maplibregl-ctrl-group';\n\n    const button = document.createElement('button');\n    button.type = 'button';\n    button.style.display = 'flex';\n    button.style.alignItems = 'center';\n    button.style.justifyContent = 'center';\n    button.style.color = '#616161';\n    button.innerHTML = UNDO_ICON_SVG;\n    button.addEventListener('click', () => this.onUndo());\n    this.container.appendChild(button);\n    this.button = button;\n    return this.container;\n  }\n\n  onRemove(): void {\n    this.container?.remove();\n    this.container = null;\n    this.button = null;\n  }\n\n  setState(canUndo: boolean, labels: UndoControlLabels): void {\n    if (!this.button) return;\n    this.button.disabled = !canUndo;\n    this.button.title = canUndo ? labels.undo : labels.nothingToUndo;\n    this.button.setAttribute('aria-label', labels.undo);\n    this.button.style.opacity = canUndo ? '1' : '0.4';\n  }\n}\n\ninterface UndoControlProps {\n  canUndo: boolean;\n  labels: UndoControlLabels;\n  onUndo: () => void;\n}\n\nexport function UndoControl({ canUndo, labels, onUndo }: UndoControlProps) {\n  const onUndoRef = useRef(onUndo);\n  onUndoRef.current = onUndo;\n\n  const control = useControl<UndoMapControl>(\n    () => new UndoMapControl(() => onUndoRef.current()),\n    { position: 'top-right' }\n  );\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    control.setState(canUndo, labels);\n  }, [control, canUndo, labels]);\n\n  return null;\n}\n\nexport default UndoControl;\n"
```

```json
 "content": "/**\n * Undo for map-driven waypoint edits (clicking the map to add a stop,\n * dragging a marker, or dragging a route vertex). Each of those records a\n * checkpoint first; this hook exposes the button state and binds Cmd/Ctrl+Z.\n */\n'use client';\n\nimport { useCallback, useEffect } from 'react';\nimport { useAppDispatch, useAppSelector } from '@/store/hooks';\n\nexport function useWaypointUndo() {\n  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();\n  const canUndo = useAppSelector((state) => state.waypoints.history.length > 0);\n\n  const undo = useCallback(() => {\n    dispatch.waypoints.undo();\n  }, [dispatch]);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {\n      if (e.key !== 'z' && e.key !== 'Z') return;\n      if (!(e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) || e.shiftKey || e.altKey) return;\n      // Leave the browser's own undo alone while the user is typing\n      const el = e.target as HTMLElement | null;\n      const tag = el?.tagName;\n      if (tag === 'INPUT' || tag === 'TEXTAREA' || el?.isContentEditable) return;\n      e.preventDefault();\n      dispatch.waypoints.undo();\n    };\n    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);\n    return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);\n  }, [dispatch]);\n\n  return { canUndo, undo };\n}\n\nexport default useWaypointUndo;\n"
}
```

```bash
feat(waypoints): undo map edits

Adding a stop by clicking the map, dragging a waypoint marker, or dragging
a route vertex now records a checkpoint first, and an undo button in the
map's control stack (plus Cmd/Ctrl+Z) restores the previous waypoint set —
which re-routes automatically. History holds the last 25 edits and resets
when a shared link replaces the whole waypoint set.
```

### CLAUDE (2026-09-01T14:32:36.009Z)

Undo is in. How it works:

**State** (`src/store/models/waypoints.ts`) — the model now carries a `history: WaypointsSnapshot[]` stack (last 25) with two reducers: `checkpoint()` records the current origin/destination/intermediates, and `undo()` pops the newest snapshot and restores it. Because `useRouting` keys off the waypoint set, an undo re-routes automatically. A shared-link restore (`setAll`) starts a fresh history, and it's never persisted or put in the share URL.

**Checkpoints** are taken immediately before each map-driven edit:
- clicking the map to set origin/destination/add a stop, and the context-menu equivalents (`useMapInteraction`)
- dragging a waypoint marker (`handleMarkerDragEnd`)
- dragging a route vertex — the checkpoint lives inside `commitDragPosition` just before the `addWaypoint`, so it's exactly one undo step per drag (the mid-drag pause and the release both go through it), and a drag that never inserts anything leaves history untouched (`RouteVertices.tsx:127`)
- the POI info-window's Start here / Add stop / Directions buttons

**UI** — `UndoControl.tsx`, a native maplibre control so it stacks with the navigation/traffic/draw buttons top-right; disabled (40% opacity, "Nothing to undo" tooltip) when the stack is empty. `useWaypointUndo` also binds Cmd/Ctrl+Z globally, skipping inputs/textareas so the browser's own text undo still works. Both labels added across all 13 full locales.

Verified in the browser: clicking the map inserted a stop (2.0 mi → 4.2 mi, 3 waypoints), the undo button then removed it and the route recalculated back to 2.0 mi / 7 min.

One gap: I could not exercise the **vertex-drag** case in Chrome — the tab's `requestAnimationFrame` was suspended (occluded window), so the hover never revealed the vertex handles and a `Runtime.evaluate` probe timed out at 45 s. If you bring the Chrome window forward I'll re-run that leg; the code path shares `commitDragPosition` with the release commit, which is the line I changed.

### CLAUDE (2026-09-01T15:18:53.335Z)

The Route Summary card no longer grows with the leg count.

- New `LegStrip` component in `RouteSummaryOverlay.tsx` renders a fixed window of **2 leg chips** flanked by prev/next `ChevronLeft`/`ChevronRight` buttons, with a `1–2 / 4` counter beside the "Route Legs" caption. Arrows step by one leg and disable at each end.
- The window start is **clamped** rather than reset, so a re-route that shortens the leg list can't leave the strip scrolled past the end.
- Chips use `flex: 1; minWidth: 0` inside a `minWidth: 0` row so they can't push the card wider; I bumped the card's `minWidth` from 256 to 300 once (static, not per-leg) so "Leg 2: 2.2 mi" fits without an ellipsis.
- Added `route.prevLegs` / `route.nextLegs` for the button labels and tooltips across all 13 locales.

Verified in the browser with a 4-leg route: card showed "Route Legs 1–2 / 4" with the left arrow disabled; clicking next advanced to "2–3 / 4" with Legs 2 and 3 and the card unchanged in size.

Committed as `fbc1f07`, not yet deployed — say the word and I'll build/push/apply.

STOP_SIGN_SVG,\n};\n\n/** Rasterises an inline SVG so it can be handed to map.addImage. */\nfunction loadIcon(svg: string): Promise<HTMLImageElement> {\n  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n    const image = new Image();\n    image.width = ICON_PX * ICON_PIXEL_RATIO;\n    image.height = ICON_PX * ICON_PIXEL_RATIO;\n    image.onload = () => resolve(image);\n    image.onerror = reject;\n    image.src = `data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8,${encodeURIComponent(svg.trim())}`;\n  });\n}\n\nconst iconLayerStyle: SymbolLayer = {\n  id: LAYER_ID,\n  type: 'symbol',\n  source: SOURCE_ID,\n  minzoom: MIN_ZOOM,\n  layout: {\n    'icon-image': ['get', 'icon'],\n    'icon-size': ['interpolate', ['linear'], ['zoom'], MIN_ZOOM, 0.35, 16, 0.5, 19, 0.7],\n    // Route furniture sits close together; never drop one for collisions\n    'icon-allow-overlap': true,\n    'icon-ignore-placement': true,\n  },\n};\n\nfunction toFeatures(\n  points: RoadPoint[],\n  icon: string\n): GeoJSON.Feature<GeoJSON.Point>[] {\n  return points.map((p) => ({\n    type: 'Feature',\n    properties: { icon },\n    geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: p.location },\n  }));\n}\n\nexport const RoadInfoMarkers: React.FC = () => {\n  const { current: mapRef } = useMap();\n  const trafficLights = useAppSelector(\n    (state) => state.route.result?.trafficLights\n  );\n  const stopSigns = useAppSelector((state) => state.route.result?.stopSigns);\n\n  const data = useMemo(\n    (): GeoJSON.FeatureCollection<GeoJSON.Point> => ({\n      type: 'FeatureCollection',\n      features: [\n function loadIcon(svg: string): Promise<HTMLImageElement> {

```bash
    .trim()
    .replace(

    );

  // backstop for a layer that asks for one at some other moment.
  const iconCache = useRef<Record<string, HTMLImageElement>>({});
  useEffect(() => {
    const map = mapRef?.getMap() as unknown as MaplibreMap | undefined;
    if (!map) return;

    let cancelled = false;

        iconCache.current[id] = image;

      }

    const addAll = () => {

    const onMissing = (e: { id: string }) => void addIcon(e.id);
    map.on('styleimagemissing', onMissing);

    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
      map.off('style.load', addAll);
      map.off('styleimagemissing', onMissing);
    };
  }, [mapRef]);
```
